title: Abelian sheaf cohomology on directed inverse limits of spectral spaces
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, every pair has a common upper bound). Let $X_i$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space], with continuous transition maps $f_{ij}:X_j\to X_i$ for $i\le j$, satisfying $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ij}f_{jk}=f_{ik}$. Assume each $f_{ij}$ is spectral, meaning that the inverse image of every quasi-compact open is quasi-compact. Let $X$ be spectral and let continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$, satisfying $f_{ij}\circ p_j=p_i$ for $i\le j$, exhibit $X$ as the inverse limit in topological spaces: the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection onto the compatible tuples and the topology is the coarsest making all $p_i$ continuous. For each $i$ let $F_i$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $X_i$. Give morphisms $\alpha_{ij}:F_i\to(f_{ij})_*F_j$ for $i\le j$, with $\alpha_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha_{ik}=(f_{ij})_*\alpha_{jk}\circ\alpha_{ij}$, using the sectionwise equality $(f_{ik})_*=(f_{ij})_*(f_{jk})_*$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Equivalently their adjoints are compatible inverse-image maps $f_{ij}^{-1}F_i\to F_j$. On $X$ form $F=\varinjlim_{i\in I}p_i^{-1}F_i$ in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with transition maps obtained by pulling back those adjoints and using $p_i=f_{ij}p_j$. Then for every $q\ge0$ the canonical pullback-and-coprojection maps induce an isomorphism of abelian groups $$\varinjlim_{i\in I}H^q(X_i,F_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X,F).$$ Here cohomology is the right-derived global sections of abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], and the transition maps on cohomology are induced by $\alpha_{ij}$ and pullback along $f_{ij}$.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, final sentence and preceding setup, specialized to a directed-set index

proof.text: Define a_ij by the canonical cohomology map on the transition f-map and b_i by that map on the adjoint of the pullback-sheaf coprojection. The normalized-map laws give identity, composition and cocone compatibility. Thus a defines the stage-cohomology diagram H and b defines a cocone c with point H^q(X,colim P). Choose the presentation isomorphisms to be identity.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, final sentence and preceding setup, specialized to a directed-set index

proof.text: For injectivity of colimit.desc H c, represent an arbitrary element by x at an index i. If its image vanishes, the cocone equation gives b_i(x)=0. Eventual-zero supplies j≥i where a_ij(x)=0. The colimit relation identifies the representative of x at i with that zero representative at j. Additivity then gives injectivity by applying this zero-kernel argument to differences.

source.place: Tag 0A37, label lemma-colimit, final sentence and preceding setup, specialized to a directed-set index

proof.text: For surjectivity, class-lift represents any y∈H^q(X,colim P) as b_i(x) for some i and x. The colimit coprojection sends x to an element whose comparison image is y. A bijective morphism of abelian groups is an isomorphism. The cocone legs and identity presentation isomorphisms give exactly the stipulated conclusion.
